|dictionary=[[Lexico]] UK English Dictionary |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]}} {{langx|az|Bakı}} {{IPA|az|bɑˈcɯ||Az-baku.ogg}}) is the [[Capital city|capital]] and [[List of cities in Azerbaijan|largest city]] of [[Azerbaijan]], as well as the largest city on the [[Caspian Sea]] and in the [[Caucasus]] region.{{Cite web |title=Seven astounding facts about the city of Baku |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/articles/2KC0g2TGpjBXGp5x5rm4KKd/seven-astounding-facts-about-the-city-of-baku |access-date=6 September 2020 |archive-date=30 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200930063703/https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/articles/2KC0g2TGpjBXGp5x5rm4KKd/seven-astounding-facts-about-the-city-of-baku |url-status=live}} Baku is {{convert|28|m|ft}} below [[sea level]], which makes it the [[List of capital cities by elevation|lowest lying national capital in the world]] and the largest city in the world below sea level. Baku lies on the southern shore of the [[Absheron Peninsula]], along the Bay of Baku. Baku's [[urban population]] is estimated at over two million people. Baku is the [[primate city]] of Azerbaijan. It is the sole metropolis in the country, and about 25% of all inhabitants of the country live in Baku's [[metropolitan area]]. Baku is divided into [[#Administrative divisions|twelve administrative raions]] and 48 townships. Among these are the townships on the islands of the [[Baku Archipelago]], as well as the industrial settlement of [[Neft Daşları]] built on oil rigs {{convert|60|km|mi|0|abbr=off}} away from Baku, in the Caspian Sea. The [[Old City (Baku)|Old City]], containing the [[Palace of the Shirvanshahs]] and the [[Maiden Tower (Baku)|Maiden Tower]], was designated as a UNESCO [[World Heritage Site]] in 2000.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/958/ |title=Walled City of Baku with the Shirvanshah's Palace and Maiden Tower |website=UNESCO |access-date=11 April 2023}} The city is the scientific, cultural, and industrial centre of Azerbaijan. Many sizeable Azerbaijani institutions have their headquarters there. In the 2010s, Baku became a venue for major international events. It hosted the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2012|57th Eurovision Song Contest]] in 2012, the [[2015 European Games]], the [[European Grand Prix]] in 2016, the 4th [[Islamic Solidarity Games]] in 2017, the [[Azerbaijan Grand Prix]] since 2017, the [[2019 UEFA Europa League Final|final]] of the [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League]], [[UEFA Euro 2020]] and the [[2024 United Nations Climate Change Conference]].{{cite news |last1=James |first1=William |title=Explainer: What is the point of a UN climate COP? |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/what-is-point-un-climate-cop-2024-11-09/ |access-date=11 November 2024 |work=Reuters}}{{cite news |last1=Khan |first1=Yusuf |title=Welcome to Baku, a City Built on Oil Hosting the World's Climate Conference |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/welcome-to-baku-a-city-built-on-oil-hosting-the-worlds-climate-conference-ba3d7e58?mod=lead_feature_below_a_pos1 |access-date=11 November 2024 |work=The Wall Street Journal}} Baku joined the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities in 2020.{{cite web|title=UNESCO Global Network of Learning cities - Baku, Azerbaijan |url=https://www.uil.unesco.org/en/learning-cities/baku |orig-date=2020 |publisher=UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning}} The [[Port of Baku|Baku International Sea Trade Port]] is capable of handling two million tonnes of general and dry bulk cargoes per year.{{Cite web |title=Port of Baku |url=http://www.worldportsource.com/ports/AZE_Port_of_Baku_2192.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721064024/http://www.worldportsource.com/ports/AZE_Port_of_Baku_2192.php |archive-date=21 July 2011 |access-date=23 December 2010 |publisher=World Port Source}} Baku is renowned for its harsh winds, reflected in its nickname, the "City of Winds".
